hints: A period is a prefix that repeats to form the string; the last repetition is allowed to be partial.
For a candidate length p, the characters after the first p must match the corresponding prefix characters.
The prefix-function value pi[n-1] is the longest matching border; p is a period exactly when pi[n-1] >= n-p.
analogy: A repeating block may run out before the end, so compare the remaining suffix with the same-length beginning of the string.
example: For abcabca, lengths 3, 6, and 7 are periods: abc repeats twice and then partially, abcabc is followed by a, and the whole string is itself a period.
complexity: O(n) time for the prefix function and the scan over lengths, and O(n) space for the prefix-function array, where n is the string length.
correctness: A length p is a period exactly when the suffix starting at p matches the prefix of length n-p. The prefix-function value pi[n-1] is the longest prefix that is also a suffix, so this match exists exactly when pi[n-1] is at least n-p. Checking every p therefore prints exactly all periods.
algorithm: Compute the prefix function pi for the string. For each length p from 1 through n, print p if pi[n-1] >= n-p. The full length n always passes; the condition allows the final repetition to be partial.
